Ugmuls 5.5e Automation · Detailed Summary

GM
Automation.

Regions, target handling, saving throws, damage and healing application, and combat tracking for the table.

Regions

Persistent areas
and recurring activities

Regions connect a spell or feature’s native activities to entry, exit, movement, and turn-start/end events. Configure individual recipes in the Spell and Region Manager, available from Module Options or the Compendium sidebar.

  • Matching activities Recipes refer to your own item’s activity names. They do not include purchased spell text or replace the item. Add the recurring save/damage activities and effects the recipe expects.
  • Region effects Assigned conditions and Active Effects follow creatures inside the area and are removed on exit. Hostile-only triggers also restrict their Region effects. Region-owned effects take priority over equivalent spell effects, preventing duplicates.
  • Once Per Turn and shared cards A target triggers once in the current combat turn. With Share Activity Card Per Turn, newly affected creatures can join the same card and linked damage roll; a new turn starts a fresh card.
  • Movement damage For areas such as Spike Growth, configured distance increments accumulate pending damage. GM plus/minus controls allow adjustments before rolling.
  • Placement and cleanup Placement helpers support attached self emanations. Concentration cleanup removes linked Regions; instantaneous areas can clear at the caster’s turn end while cards remain available.

Turn triggers require active combat and initiative. Six starter recipes provide settings and activity names for review.

Targeting

Smart area selection.
Adjust from the card.

Region areas use smart targeting based on the spell card’s activity settings. Enemy, Friend / Ally, and Select Targets determine which creatures inside the area are included, with enemy and ally selection relative to the caster.

  • Select Targets: confirm your choices. When the spell allows target selection, a confirmation prompt lets you review the creatures, add targets from the map, and remove names before proceeding.
  • Metamagic: choose as you cast. Sorcerers automatically receive applicable cast-time Metamagic options, such as Transmuted Spell and Careful Spell, alongside other supported choices. Make your selections during casting, and the automation carries those choices into the spell’s saves and damage without extra follow-up steps after the cast.
  • Retarget: adjust on the spot. Use Retarget on the chat card to update the cast’s recorded targets from your current selection. Linked hit, miss, and saving-throw results update with the revised targeting, including hit and miss checks after an AC change. Undo any applied damage before making corrections that need to change HP.
Rolls & Damage / Healing

Damage, saves,
and corrections

The next roll, ready when you need it

The module prompts users when it’s time to roll, including damage, saving throws, and concentration checks. Prompts go to the connected player who owns the character, with the GM available when they aren’t connected. Less hunting for the next button, more time keeping the game moving.

Pending rolls keep you in the loop

Someone preparing a big Fireball with Metamagic? The chat card shows that the cast is underway while they work through their choices, then updates as the rolls resolve. The GM can follow what’s happening while the player finishes preparing the spell.

Closed a save or damage prompt by mistake? The GM or an eligible owner can click ---pending--- on the card to reopen it and finish the roll. The result fills that same card once the dice animation finishes.

Roll adjustments: keep the dice you rolled

Targeted the wrong creature or missed an advantage setting? Supported chat-card adjustments keep the original dice and bonuses, so fixing the target doesn’t mean losing that natural 20 to a fresh roll. If an adjustment needs another die, only the extra die is rolled. Undo any applied damage before making a correction that changes it.

Advantage / Normal / Disadvantage

Completed attack and save cards offer mode corrections while retaining their original d20 and bonuses. An additional d20 rolls only when needed and is then cached. Results update after the animation.

Normal / Critical damage

Supported attack damage cards can convert between Normal and Critical, retaining cached rolls and handling Savage Attacker’s complete dice sets.

Apply and Undo

GM Undo Damage and Undo Healing reverse the card’s tracked HP and temporary-HP applications. Undo Effect removes newly applied effects or restores refreshed effects, preserving later applications from other cards. Manual reapplication restores the corresponding Undo control.

Applied damage locks linked roll/critical adjustments. Undo all outstanding applications first, adjust, then apply again. Stunning Strike and Grapple effect Undo unlock their own rolled saves independently of weapon damage; automatic Stunned failures do not offer a dice-mode correction.

Undo requires recorded applications; older history cannot be reconstructed. Keep an active GM connected to record player applications.

GM NPC & Damage / Healing

Automatic resolution.
Manual decisions stay available.

  • Automatically Roll GM NPC Saves Resolves prompted saves for GM-run NPCs using native recommended advantage/disadvantage. Player-owned NPCs remain manual. Magic Resistance and supported condition sources combine normally.
  • Auto Apply Damage Applies attack damage to confirmed hits and waits for eligible saves and dice animations before applying save damage. Resistance, vulnerability, immunity, and supported save rules still apply.

    Give reactions room to happen. Applying damage closes most roll-correction and reaction options until that damage is undone. Auto Apply can speed up lower-level play when reactions are uncommon. Once you have a Bard, a Sorcerer, or a pesky Wizard ready with Silvery Barbs, consider turning it off so the table can finish those decisions before clicking Apply.

  • Auto Apply Healing A separate setting applies healing and temporary HP after the completed roll. Enable it independently of automatic damage.
  • Auto Apply Saved Effects Applies configured effects from saving-throw outcomes, including effects set to apply on a successful save. Stunning Strike and Grapple use their own save results. See the Auto Apply Damage caution above: applying effects can also close related corrections until those effects are undone. Effect reversals are usually less common than damage reversals, but manual application may suit a table with frequent reactions.
  • Autoapply Status on Hit Applies the attack activity’s configured effects to confirmed hit targets.
  • The GM controls the final step. Applying damage is the action’s end state. If something needs changing, the GM can use Undo Damage and Undo Effect to reverse recorded applications. Once the relevant damage and effects are undone, eligible class features, reactions, and roll adjustments become available again. Make the correction, then reapply from the card.

Damage, healing, saved effects, and on-hit effects have separate settings, so you can choose how much to automate. Keep an active GM connected for applications to actors players do not own.

Automations → Common

Combat resource
and save tracking

  • Bonus Action - used Tracks native bonus-action uses for all active combat participants and resets at the token’s next turn start.
  • Reaction - used Tracks reaction activities and manual off-turn uses for all combat participants. Further reactions are blocked until the marker is disabled, deleted, or cleared at the next turn start. Saves, linked damage, and automated Region triggers stay available.
  • Consumed Spell Slot Tracks character actors during combat and resets at the end of the current turn. Cantrips, free casts, and non-spell slot expenditures are excluded. These resource trackers do not run out of combat.
  • Magic Resistance Recognizes the feature when recommending saves against spells or magical features. It combines with other sources and integrates with Automated Conditions.
